## Overview[]

Unlocked by giving Iron Fortress to the Sculptor. Sold by Blackhat Badger for 1600 1600 in Ashina Castle near the Old Grave Sculptor's Idol. Costs 1 **1** Spirit Emblem to use. 

Sekiro Shadows Die Twice Iron Fortress location (iron umbrella)

Sekiro Shadows Die Twice Iron Fortress location (iron umbrella)

The Loaded Umbrella is the only primarily defensive Prosthetic Tool within Sekiro's arsenal and does a wondrous job at it. The basic version alone could protect against most attacks save for Sweeping, Fire, Lightning and Terror attacks. Pressing the Prosthetic Tool button will have Sekiro draw the Umbrella and spread it out. Attacks that make contact during the animation are Deflected. The timing for deflection is easier than that of Deflecting with Kusabimaru. Holding the Prosthetic button will instead have Sekiro turtle down with the Umbrella, allowing players to reposition while guarded from most form of attacks. It should be remembered that Guarding with the umbrella does not prevent the posture bar from filling up, the guard will likewise break once the bar is filled.

The **Projected Force** Prosthetic Martial Art allows Sekiro to do a powerful, stagger-resistant cross-slash with the umbrella's metallic frame from the turtle position; this attacks ends the guard, and reenacting the umbrella will consume Spirit Emblems. The same Martial Art also adds a projectile mechanic to the umbrella: after guarding/deflecting enough projectile attack, the umbrella will begin to emit smoke, from whence Sekiro can launch a powerful projectile attack that launches straighr into the locked on target by executing the aforementioned cross-slash attack. This projectile can be stored for later use as long as players do not switch Prosthetic Tool.

The **Magnet** upgrade adds an umbrella spinning move that can be executed by pressing the Guard button while the umbrella is unfolded. Attacks making contact while the umbrella is spun will be perfectly deflected. This spinning move has a decent animation frame and thus is not hard to pull off. It also omits the player from needing to fold and unfold to deflect with the umbrella.

The **Phoenix's Lilac Umbrella** upgrade keeps the spinning mechanic from previous upgrade and adds the ability to guard/deflect Apparition attacks and prevent Terror build-up. In addition, the Projected Force allows this version of the Umbrella to be coated in an energy similar with the effect of Divine Confetti when used for the Cross-Slash attack (not the projectile), dealing massive Vitality and Posture damage to Apparition type enemies. These set of featues make this umbrella particularly useful against Shichimen Warrior and Headless. Note that the umbrella does not protect against Shichimen Warrior's AoE terror field attack, because the terror energy erupts from the floor, an angle of which the umbrella does not protect.

The **Suzaku's Lotus** upgrade works under the same principle as Phoenix's Lilac, but in the case of Fire-based attacks. This makes the Umbrella useful against several late game enemies like the Red Guard Cannon-wielder and Riflemen who uses powerful Fire projectiles and the Demon of Hatred. Note that the Projected Force attacks of this umbrella does not build up Burn status on enemies despite the flaming animation. 

## Ability[]

**(Hold) Shelter** : Spread the Loaded Umbrella to guard from attacks in all directions. You can also move with the fan deployed, and it will continue to block lighter attacks as you move. 

**(Release the moment enemy attack lands) Umbrella Deflect** : Spread the Umbrella to deflect enemy attacks. Umbrella deflects are easier to time than sword deflects. 

**(Press Guard while keeping the Umberella on):** Fold and unfold the umbrella for another possible deflect.

**(Press Guard while keeping the Umberella on):** Fold and unfold the umbrella for another possible deflect. 

**(Press Guard while keeping the Umberella's upgraded version on):** Spin. Strikes that make contact while the umberella is spun will be deflected. Spinning cost 1 Spirit Emblem.

**Nightjars** are a normal enemy in Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice. They are most commonly found in Ashina Castle, Sunken Valley and Ashina Depths. 

## Brown Nightjar[]

## Brown Nightjar

First encountered on the roofs of Ashina Castle. 

One next to the fallen head of a Buddha statue in Riven Cave, along with one in black uniform. 

### Behaviour and Tactics[]

  * **Sickles Throw** : he leaps around while throwing a pair of homing sickles.
  * **Cross Slash** : lunges forward, slashing both sickles.
  * **Leaping Slice** : leaps up then come crashing down with a slice.



* * *

While they are perceptive, it is possible to perform a Stealth Deathblow on most Brown nightjar. Using nearby rooftops, grapple and climb to an area some distance behind the enemy, then sneak up on them to perform the deathblow.

However, there are some nightjar who cannot be snuck around. In such situations, it is helpful to make frequent use of the Chasing Slice ability in combination with the Loaded Shuriken prosthetic. This will help mitigate the nightjar's mobility, which can prove problematic. in many cases, it is possible to corner these enemies and attack them repeatedly. this will prevent them from performing any attacks, effectively ending the fight. 

## Grey Nightjar[]

## Grey Nightjar

Three are found right below the room of Isshin Ashina before the invasion. 

### Behaviour and Tactics[]

## Grey Nightjar[]

## Grey Nightjar

Three are found right below the room of Isshin Ashina before the invasion. 

### Behaviour and Tactics[]

  * **Leaping Whirlwind** : leaps backwards for a brief moment, then he lunges forwards spinning the weapon.
  * **Twin Cyclones** : hops to the left then spins his weapon twice before leaping backwards.
  * **Whirlwind** : hops to the right then spins the weapon, and may follow up with _Overhead Cut_ and a spin.
  * **Overhead Cut** : spins in the air then comes crashing down with a cut. When the target is too far away, he spins directly at him and does this attack twice.
  * **Nimble Strike** : jumps to the left then quickly lunges forth, slashing once.
  * **Somersault** : slashes from below then leaps backwards.

## Black Nightjar

They await on kites for their target to approach on the roofs of Ashina Castle. One next to the head of a fallen Buddha statue in Riven Cave accompanied by another Nightjar wearing brown uniform. 

Later they are also found in Ashina Castle after the invasion. 

### Behaviour and Tactics[]

When attacking from the kites, they signal their charge with a loud continuous shout as they home in at their target. 

  * **Fiery Weapon** : throws gunpowder into the air that explodes, engulfing his weapon in flames.
  * **Leaping Whirlwind** : leaps forward, spinning his weapon.
  * **Overhead Cut** : turning, he smashes down his weapon in an arc.
  * **Whirlwind** : standing still, he spins his weapon around in a wide arc, finishing in a jump and final spin.
  * **Somersault** : leaps backwards or to the side to maneuver.
  * **Spin Slash** : in a backwards leap, he spins his weapon around in circles.

## Description[]

## Anayama the Peddler

**Anayama the Peddler** (物売りの穴山), is a bandit turned merchant. He had an encounter with Wolf in the Hirata Estate, when his band of thieves led by Juzou the Drunkard sieged the place. 

Anayama seeks now to expand his business, but has run short on money, so he offers to sell Wolf some important information about the night they met and a peculiar treasure of the Hirata Estate in exchange for a few Sen. 

He'll ask Sekiro to first discover what the Ashina Samurai are in desperate need of and then to bring him a strong man who's willing to pillage the corpses of the battlefields. 

When the final attack of the Central Forces hits Ashina, he'll lose his entire stock to the invading hordes and his life too. 

## Location[]

When the final attack of the Central Forces hits Ashina, he'll lose his entire stock to the invading hordes and his life too. 

## Location[]

  * Outskirts Wall - Stairway: before the Sculptor's Idol, he sits beyond the gate guarded by the Cannoneer. 
    * If Kotaro joined him, during the final invasion of Ashina Castle and Outskirts, he'll be found on the other side of the gate were he used to be.
  * Estate Path: past the gate behind the two Bandits shouting at Hirata residents to surrender, before the first two Shield-Wielding Bandits.



## Progression #1 ("That Night")[]

### Ashina Outskirts (Outskirts Wall - Stairway)[]

Talk to Anayama and purchase his informations for 10 10\. 

_(Optional)_ Pay 20 20 to buy the Flame Barrel Memo. If Wolf is already in possession of the Flame Barrel, Anayama will give him Oil [x2]. 

Once the area is reloaded, Anayama will have some merch to sell and upon leaving him, he'll ask Sekiro to find out what the Ashina Samurai need.

Once the area is reloaded, Anayama will have some merch to sell and upon leaving him, he'll ask Sekiro to find out what the Ashina Samurai need. 

## Progression #2 (Salt)[]

### Ashina Castle (Old Grave)[]

Eavesdrop on the Ashina Samurai and Ashina Rifleman on the bridge to the Great Serpent Shrine. 

### Ashina Outskirts (Outskirts Wall - Stairway)[]

Report back to Anayama and reload the area: he will have new items in his stock and, as Wolf's leaving, he'll tell the shinobi that he's looking for a strong man to help him take weapons and armors from the corpses of fallen soldiers. 

## Progression #3 (Business Will Continue)[]

### Senpou Temple (Shugendo)[]

Retrieve the Red and White Pinwheel on the cliff before the Armored Warrior. 

### Senpou Temple (Senpou Temple, Mt. Kongo)[]

Talk to Kotaro and give him the Pinwheel: this will unlock the option to send him to Anayama. 

### Ashina Outskirts (Outskirts Wall - Stairway)[]

Talk to Kotaro and give him the Pinwheel: this will unlock the option to send him to Anayama. 

### Ashina Outskirts (Outskirts Wall - Stairway)[]

With Kotaro by his side, Anayama will now have new products in his inventory. 

### Fountainhead Palace (Fountainhead Palace)[]

Upon defeating the Corrupted Monk, the Dragon's Tally Board she drops will unlock new items at every merchant, Anayama included. 

### Ashina Outskirts (Outskirts Wall - Stairway)[]

After the Divine Dragon is defeated, Ashina will be assaulted one last time by the Central Forces. Anayama, having lost everything to the invaders, offers Wolf his last piece of product, his Promissory Note that discounts the cost of items when purchasing from merchants, for 1 1\. 

## Progression #4 (The Three-Story Pagoda)[]

### Hirata Estate (Estate Path)[]

If talked in the Hirata Estate memory, Anayama will tell Wolf of a three-story pagoda that might contain a valuable treasure. 

## Behaviour and Tactic[]

## Behaviour and Tactic[]

  * **Drag Swing** : drags the axe behind him to gain momentum then swings it above his head in a strong blow.
  * **Running Swing** : closes distance to his attacker and swings the axe low quickly.
  * **Shaft Hit** : hits the attacker with the shaft of the axe.
  * **Shove** : shoves his attacker with his fist, knocking them back.
  * **Swing** : swings the axe horizontally, followed by a vertical swing.
  * **Upperhead Swing** : brings the axe down from above his head in a swing.



Fights exactly like an Axe-Wielding Bandit.

## Notes[]

  * If Anayama is killed in Hirata Estate, he'll also disappear from Ashina Outskirts.
  * When one completes his questline with the Promissory Note already in their inventory, a prompt will ask if the player wants to purchase a Dragon's Blood Droplet for 1 1, but if they accept the item received will be a Divine Grass.
  * With Patch 1.04 the price of his informations was decreased from 50 50 to 10 10 and of the Flame Barrel Memo from 100 100 to 20 20.
  * The only merchant alongside Blackhat Badger to sell Yashariku's Sugars.

* The Phantom Kunai becomes available for 4500 4500 in the Offering Box next to Hanbei after the final invasion of Ashina Castle and Outskirts by the Central Forces, if not purchased prior. It's not necessary to unlock the Kunai from Anayama to have it appear in the Offering Box. 
    * Acquiring this item is a necessary step to unlock the "Master of the Prosthetic" trophy.


  * The only merchant who sells an infinite supply of Ako's Sugars.
  * His Dragonrot infection doesn't affect his past self in Hirata Estate.
  * It's possible to complete his questline even if he's infected with Dragonrot, as long as Kotaro is sent to him.
  * Can't be harmed while infected with Dragonrot or at the end of his questline.



## Trivia[]

## Trivia[]

  * His Rot Essence refers to him as "Newcomer", but in japanese it's actually "man who aims to expand his business" (商いの昇り人).
  * His eyepatch is actually a seashell and he bears a tattoo of three black circles on his left lower arm.
  * His full name is **Anayama Matabei** (穴山又兵衛), according to the description of his Promissory Note.
  * One of the few NPC that can be attacked and killed.
  * If he's turned hostile after Kotaro joined him, the latter will simply crawl in fear as Anayama fights off Wolf.
  * If the Flame Barrel Memo isn't purchased prior to his death at the hands of the Central Forces, it may be randomly dropped by one of the Agents nearby his location.

**(HOLD GUARD + ATTACK) Perform a Shadowrush attack with extended range** : Leaping in the air costs Spirit Emblems.

An evolution of Shadowrush, this is a Secret Technique of the Ashina Mushin Compound Style. After leaping into the skies with Shadowrush, allows one to perform a spinning sword attack as they descend. Pierce, fly, and then dive back down. Jumping off the enemy costs Spirit Emblems.

Redirect to:

  * Sunken Valley#Sunken Valley Passage

## Great Serpent

Two enormous snakes, encountered in different areas of the game. 

The first one is come across in the Underbridge Valley where Wolf can stab him in the eye by entering the palanquin. 

He is later encountered in the Sunken Valley where it destroys the bridge to the Gun Fort. 

Lastly, it can be killed once Wolf has flown the Kite and grappled through to the other side of the valley from Senpou Temple, obtaining the Fresh Serpent Viscera. 

The second Great Serpent is encountered in the Sunken Valley Passage on the way to a shrine holding the Dried Serpent Viscera.   


## First Encounter, Ashina Outskirts[]

Hide until the serpent draws near, then Deathblow it in the eye. This will not outright kill it though, but cause him to thrash around violently, giving enough time to escape the valley. 

## Second Encounter, Sunken Valley[]

## Second Encounter, Sunken Valley[]

As Wolf attempts to cross the bridge to the Gun Fort, the Serpent will destroy the bridge, causing Wolf to fall into the lake below. hide in the reeds and reach the cave ahead to escape. 

## Third Encounter, Senpou Temple Kite[]

After obtaining the Puppeteer Ninjutsu, Wolf is able to puppeteer the Rat near the kite mechanism at the beginning of Senpou Temple, then grapple through the kite, to access a plank from which he can plunge onto the head of the Serpent, killing it and obtaining the Fresh Serpent Viscera. 

## The Second Great Serpent, in the Sunken Valley Passage[]

## The Second Great Serpent, in the Sunken Valley Passage[]

It is in the Sunken Valley Passage, entered from nearby the Toxic Memorial Mob. The cave is also guarded by several Rock Divers and Lizards. It reacts rather violently to any intrusion to its domain, hitting the nearby poison geysers. In order to enter the shrine, use the Puppeteer Ninjutsu on the nearby Monkey to distract the serpent. Alternatively, grapple below the serpent's head then immediately fall to dodge his attack, then grapple back on, or use Mist Raven to dodge the attack and run into the shrine. This Serpent cannot be killed.

## Trivia[]

  * During the first encounter with the Orochi, Wolf can escape the valley without stabbing the Serpent in the eye, but it is much more difficult.
  * When plunging on the Orochi from above at the third encounter but failing to do the second Deathblow, it'll eat Wolf without doing damage and takes him to the cave where the second Serpent is in the Sunken Valley Passage. 
    * This might suggest that the orochi shares one body, Wolf being eaten by one head and ending up coming out from the other end.

## Overview[]

A latent skill that does not belong to a tree, unlocked by defeating the Armoured Warrior in Senpou Temple.

## Mist Noble

The **Mist Noble** is a frail creature dressed in traditional noble garb, playing the flute in a closed off temple in the Hidden Forest. Entry to this temple requires a detour past Tokujiro the Glutton and through a hole in the roof. Defeating the noble will dissipate all the mist in the area along with all the ghost soldiers, revealing it to be an illusion spell. 

## Behaviors and Tactics[]

  * **Weak Punches** : throws two weak punches with a short delay in between.
  * **Flute Stab** : raises the flute in his left hand and plunges it after a medium delay.
  * **Bite** : crawls forward while using his long neck to bite down twice.



* * *

It is possible to perform a stealth attack for the first Deathblow. Upon entering the house, sneak along the beams until standing over the boss, then jump on him. After this, attack aggressively to deal as much damage as possible right away. It is possible to use Prosthetics here as well, but should not be necessary.

### Burn[]  
  
---  
| Being hit by too many fire-based attacks will eventually apply the Burn status abnormality. Guarding fire attacks does not prevent the Burn gauge from rising. While burning, flames are visible on one's body, and will prevent the regeneration of Posture and will gradually damage Vitality for the duration.   
  
## Effect[]

Burn takes 1% Vitality per second for 10 seconds, for a total of 10% maximum Vitality. It also halts Posture recovery. 

## How to cure Burn[]

Burn takes 1% Vitality per second for 10 seconds, for a total of 10% maximum Vitality. It also halts Posture recovery. 

## How to cure Burn[]

  * Dousing Powder and Ministry Dousing Powder cure Burn and increase Burn resistance by 60%/80% for 30 seconds and reduce fire damage by 40/60%.
  * The Withered Red Gourd, while it doesn't heal active Burn status abnormality, increases Burn resistance by 70% for 30 seconds and reduces fire damage by 50%.
  * Divine Grass cures Burn and fully restores Vitality.



## Enemies that inflict Burn[]

  * Torch-Wielding Bandit
  * Archer Bandit
  * Black Nightjar
  * Lesser Centipede
  * Central Force Flametrooper

### Poison[]  
  
---  
| Repeatedly getting hit by poison-based attacks will apply the "Poison" status abnormality. Guarding such attacks does not prevent Poison from accumulating. Poison affects the body and mind when it enters the body, gradually reducing Vitality over time.   
  
## Effect[]

Poison is a status effect that lasts for 40 seconds. Depending on the amount of maximum vitality, it can deplete from a third to almost the entire vitality. 

## How to cure Poison[]

  * Antidote Powder cures Poison and increases Poison resistance by 70% for 30 seconds.
  * The Green Mossy Gourd, while it doesn't heal active Poison status abnormality, increases Poison resistance by 70% for 30 seconds.
  * Divine Grass cures Poison and fully restores Vitality.
  * Contact Medicine inflicts a weak form of Poison, making others ineffective.



## Enemies that inflict Poison[]

  * Lizard
  * Rat
  * Archer Bandit (Altered Hirata Estate memory only)
  * Interior Ministry Agent

### Terror[]  
  
---  
| Taking damage from apparition-type enemies will fill the mind and body with Terror. Guarding such attacks does not prevent Terror from accumulating. Those overcome with Terror are known to die.   
  
## Effect[]

Terror is a lethal status effect that will kill Sekiro once the status gauge is full. 

## How to cure Terror[]

Terror is a lethal status effect that will kill Sekiro once the status gauge is full. 

## How to cure Terror[]

  * Pacifying Agent cures Terror build-up and increases Terror resistance by 50% for 30 seconds.
  * The Mottled Purple Gourd cures Terror build-up and increases Terror resistance by 50% for 30 seconds.
  * Divine Grass cures Terror build-up and fully restores Vitality.

### Shock[]  
  
---  
| If standing on the ground while struck by a lightning attack, the status abnormality "Shock" is inflicted. This occurs regardless of whether the attack was guarded or not. Shock causes electricity to run through one's body, dealing huge damage to Vitality and also stunning them briefly.   
  
## Effect[]

If Sekiro's feet are on the ground and he takes a lightning attack, he will take a massive Vitality and Posture damage, the amount of which varies depending on his vitality. 

## How to cure Shock[]

  * Eel Liver cures Shock and increases Shock resistance by 50% for 30 seconds.
  * Divine Grass cures Shock and fully restores Vitality.



## Enemies that inflict Shock[]

  * Okami Swordsman
  * Okami Juggler
  * Palace Dog



### Mini-Bosses[]

## How to inflict Shock[]

#### Lightning Reversal:[]

## How to inflict Shock[]

#### Lightning Reversal:[]

Lightning surges through the bodies of those with their feet on the ground, instantly paralyzing them. A secret technique exists to catch lightning in one's blade while in mid-air, and send it back.

### Enfeeblement[]  
  
---  
| Syphons youth out of the target, restricting his agile movements to only a slow limping, weak attack and the inability to use any items or prosthetic tools. It also greatly reduces his health and disables resurrection.   
  
## Effect[]

Enfeeblement is an unique statues effect inflicted by only one enemy. When the status gauge is full from playing the flute, Sekiro becomes old and infirm, unable to use prosthetics or items, with low health and weak attack. If killed, Sekiro can't resurrect. Once cured, the full health gauge is restored but low health remains. 

## How to cure Enfeeblement[]

## How to cure Enfeeblement[]

  * Kill the Palace Noble that inflicted it and perform a Deathblow on him.
  * Wait for its effect to run out (30 seconds).
  * Reaching a Sculptor's Idol and resting.



## Enemies that inflict Enfeeblement[]

  * Palace Noble

## Description[]

## Blackhat Badger

**Blackhat Badger** (黒笠のムジナ) is a merchant hiding inside an house near the Old Grave of Ashina Castle. 

He will later appear in Senpou Temple, where he'll employ Wolf's help to fly a kite so that he could cross the valley. He'll be then found in the Sunken Valley Cavern, mourning over the tomb of his child. 

He will be last found back in Ashina Castle, after the final invasion of the Central Forces: fatally wounded while defending a kid from the invaders, he'll gift Sekiro his precious Mibu Pilgrimage Balloon. 

## Location[]

  * Old Grave: on the second floor of the building just below the Sculptor's Idol.
  * Senpou Temple, Mt. Kongo: on the cliff overlooking the Senpou Assassin guarding the kite machinery.
  * Sunken Valley Cavern: just before the Sculptor's Idol.
  * Old Grave: a few feet away from the building where he was initially found, laying against a tree.

## Progression #1[]

### Ashina Castle (Upper Tower - Ashina Dojo)[]

Climb to the top of the castle and defeat Genichiro.

Grapple onto the kite to cross the valley and reach the Sunken Valley Cavern.

## Behaviour and Tactics[]

* **Perilous Grab** :: jumps up then attempts to catch Wolf. If it connects, he jumps at Wolf and twists his head back, dealing a great amount of damage.
  * **Poison Splash** :: empties a satchel of poison in front of himself creating a pool on the ground.
  * **Chasing Slice** : moves to the side with a wide slash.
  * **Chasing Stab** : moves forward swiftly with a stab of his dagger.
  * **Dart** : rolls sideway and then spits a splinter.
  * **Evasive Somersault** : rolls to either side, evading attacks.
  * **Evasive Spin** : spins in the air to the side.
  * **Jumping Stab** : jumps towards his target with a stab.
  * **Jumping Uppercut** : jumps up, slashing his dagger upwards.
  * **Slash** : slices with his dagger horizontally, sometimes twice.



Fights like a Rat.

## Notes[]

* Even if not talked to, he'll leave the Old Grave for Senpou Temple once the first invasion of Ashina Castle is triggered, leaving behind the Iron Fortress in his original spot and unlocking the Anti-air Deathblow Text for 2200 2200 in the Offering Box near Hanbei.
  * If Badger is killed prior to its purchase, the Iron Fortress will become available for 2400 2400 in the Offering Box near Hanbei.
  * If Badger is killed prior to its purchase, the Anti-air Deathblow Text will become available for 2200 2200 in the Offering Box near Hanbei once the first invasion of Ashina Castle is triggered.
  * He's the only merchant to sell Yashariku's Sugar alongside Anayama.
  * Unlike other endgame items, his Mibu Pilgrimage Balloon works like a regular consumable and as such can only be used once.
  * Can't be harmed while affected by Dragonrot or at the end of his questline.

## In-Game Description[]

A technique designed to stop cold any enemies that leap high in the air. Allows one to exploit an enemy's vulnerability in the air by jumping toward them and performing a sudden Deathblow. The perfect skill for Shinobi looking to turn the tables on airborne enemies.   
---  
  
## Availability[]

  * Unlocked by purchasing the Anti-air Deathblow Text from Blackhat Badger at the Old Grave. 
    * If Badger is dead or at Senpou Temple, it's available for 2200 2200 at the Offering Box near Hanbei once the first invasion of Ashina Castle is triggered.



## Overview[]

Allows to perform a deathblow on certain enemies by jumping toward them when they leap high into the air. 

The following enemies are susceptible to this Shinobi Martial Art: 

  * Rooster
  * Unarmed Monkey
  * Monkey Warrior
  * Dual Naginata Senpou Monk
  * Okami Swordsman
  * Okami Juggler
  * Shichimen Warrior
  * Okami Leader Shizu



## Ability[]

## Ability[]

**(ATTACK near an enemy high up in the air) Anti-air Deathblow** : Perform a Deathblow on an airborne enemy. 

## Trivia[]

  * The only Shinobi Martial Art that doesn't belong to a Skill Tree.

## In-Game Description[]

Sugar candy made in the Senpou Temple, imbued with the blessing of Ako. Temporarily boosts posture damage dealt. Bite the candy and assume the Ako stance to receive the blessing of inhuman spirits. The spirits embody excess karma. One must bite down hard on the candy and endure what has been brought to pass.  |

## Overview[]

Unlocked by giving the Large Fan to the Sculptor. It is found by a Buddha statue after defeating Long-arm Centipede Giraffe. 

Sekiro Where to find Large Fan


Divine Abduction is an auxiliary Prosthetic Tool, but one that can easily turn the tide of difficult battles when used properly. The basic use of this Tool is done in two simple steps: Players must first gather a vortex of golden wind by pressing the Prosthetic button. This wind will linger sround Sekiro for a short time before it vanishes on its own. Taking hits from any source will also dispel the wind, cancelling the window to do the next step. When opportunity prompts and the wind still linger around Sekiro, players should press the Prosthetic button again to have Sekiro create a huge vortex that will make most but the strongest enemy within 360 degree of mid-range proximity to him turned on their back, making them vulnerable to backstab Deathblow and by extension, Ninjutsu techniques that otherwise can be achieved only through stealth or the Leap Over martial art. It is important to remember that the Spirit Emblem consumption for this Prosthetic Tool takes place during the vortex gathering, not the release, thus rapid trial and error is ill-advised. 

The **Living Force** Martial Art allows players to imbue the wind's power to Kusabimaru after gathering the vortex, cancelling the vortex release in exchange for a swift blow with similar effect to one opponent. This alternative method of Divine Abduction is preferable when facing a single opponent or wanting to make a powerful puppet with the Puppeteer Ninjutsu to help in a huge confrontation. 

It is useful to note that monks of Senpou Temple would "die" instantly if caught by the golden vortex release. This is possibly a nod towards legends of Tengu committing **divine abduction** towards temple monks who forsake their responsibilities.

**Double Divine Abduction** upgrade allows players cast two vortex release from one gathering for the same Spirit Emblem cost. The upgrade also allows player to cast one vortex release or do the Living Force attack should Sekiro got hit once during the gathering phase, given the attack is not powerful enough to knock Sekiro off his feet, which would dispel the vortex completely despite the upgrade's bonus. 

**Golden Vortex** upgrade keeps the feature from previous upgrade while adding the effect of making enemy yield extra loot when caught by the vortex's effect. This extra loot effect only works once to any one enemy until they are respawned through resting. It is also important to note while it is the most complete version effects-wise, Golden Vortex cost 4 Spirit Emblems as opposed to other variant's 3 to use. 

## Ability[]

**Gathering Vortex** : Use the fan of leaves to wrap yourself in whirling winds. Costs 3 **3** Spirit Emblems to use.

## Ability[]

**Gathering Vortex** : Use the fan of leaves to wrap yourself in whirling winds. Costs 3 **3** Spirit Emblems to use. 

**(While using Gathering Vortex) Divine Abduction** : Release the winds around the enemy, making them face the opposite direction. Aside from certain strong enemies, they will lose sight of you and become momentarily vulnerable to a Deathblow.

## Mibu Village[]

The village lays deep within **Ashina Depths** and is shrouded in a dense fog. The denizens of the village are ghastly in appearance. 

At one time, the forests of pine trees in the area always appeared to be smoldering. This acted as a landmark to find one's way to the village. In time though, the villagers came to loathe the flames and destroyed the trees. Some defended the flame though, and were equally loathed. 

After defeating Corrupted Monk, Nightjar apparitions appear in Mibu Village near the plantation, and near the entrance of the village.

## In-Game Description[]

An iron barrel the spews fire. Can be fitted to the Shinobi Prosthetic to become a Prostheitc Tool.  
It is difficult to control the rage-filled-Red-eyes with the power of man alone.  
However, a fire-based weapon could be a means of resisting them. They are said to fear fire above all else.  |   
---|---  
  
## Availability[]

Found in a bonfire at Hirata Estate, next to a bonfire surrounded by bandits, to the right of the Estate Path Sculptor's Idol. 

## Overview[]

Unlocks the Flame Vent Prosthetic Tool when given to the Sculptor at the Dilapidated Temple. 

## Notes[]

## Overview[]

Unlocks the Flame Vent Prosthetic Tool when given to the Sculptor at the Dilapidated Temple. 

## Notes[]

  * If the Young Lord's Bell Charm isn't retrieved prior to the final invasion of Ashina Castle and Outskirts by the Central Forces, this item won't become available in the Offering Box next to Hanbei and it won't be obtainable for the rest of the playthrough, since the Timid Maid will be found dead.
  * Unlike for the rest of already acquired Tools that gets replaced by Bundled Jizo Statue, a Fistful of Ash will be found in place of this item in New Game Plus.

White Spirit Emblems harbor the souls of the dead. Only a shinobi could find use for such a thing.  |   
---|---  
  
Required for using Prosthetic Tools and and some Combat Arts. It's essentially a universal ammunition type, awarded for defeating enemies Sekiro removes from the world and consumed by the prosthetic whenever it's used. 

Spirit emblems are awarded for defeating enemies and can be found throughout the world, where they will float towards the Wolf upon getting close enough to them. They are first seen after acquiring the first shinobi prosthetic. Spirit Emblems can also be brought from any Sculptor's Idol. The starting price is ten Sen per Emblem, but by completing certain game events, the price will go to 30 and then 50, however Wolf will also be acquiring more Sen from enemies.

The maximum amount that can be carried is 15, but can be increased to 20 by acquiring the following Skills: A Shinobi's Karma - Body, A Shinobi's Karma - Mind, Sculptor's Karma - Blood, Sculptor's Karma - Scars and A Beast's Karma. If the Wolf is carrying the maximum amount, additional Spirit Emblems will be automatically send to the storage box, and resting at an Idol, will restore the carry stock.

Redirect to:

  * Loaded Umbrella#Loaded Umbrella - Magnet

A piece of resin that contains a continuously smoldering flame. Can be used to upgrade the Flame Vent.  
The resin was found in a black pine within the forests of Mibu Village. The ever-smoldering flames acted as a landmark to find one's way to the village. In time the villagers came to loathe the flames, and the black pines were lost. Those who defended the flame were equally loathed.  |   
---|---  
  
Found atop a roof in Mibu Village at the end of a road branching off to a secluded area. After collecting, the villagers will rise from the ground, ambushing Wolf. For further information on this item's location, speak to Basket Wearer Shosuke, who will give Wolf directions to reach the upgrade material. 

Unlocks the Okinaga's Flame Vent Prosthetic Tool upgrade when given to the Sculptor at the Dilapidated Temple.

## Rooster

**Rooster** is a normal enemy in Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice, They are first encountered next to the Outskirts Wall - Stairway Sculptor's Idol. Some found in the Hidden Forest, and also surrounding a house in Hirata Estate. 

## Behaviour and Tactics[]

  * **Aerial Strike** : leaps into the ground, attacking with its feet.
  * **Peck** : attacks once or twice with its beak.



* * *

Its Aerial Strike can do a lot of damage early game, but one parry will render the bird defenseless.   


  * Ashina Outskirts

  * Hidden Forest, Mibu Village

## In-Game Description[]

A tattered note written by Anayama. Seems to be from some years ago.  
  
"Lucrative info #36.  
When we broke into Hirata Estate, we found a barrel that spewed flame. The boys lit a roaring bonfire with it and made merry with the drink. Must have been a shinobi's tool."  |   
---|---  
  
## Availability[]

  * Sold by Anayama the Peddler for 20 20, after paying him 10 10 for some information.
  * Dropped by Anayama in Ashina Outskirts, if he's killed prior to the purchase.


  * If it's not purchased and Anayama dies in the final siege of Ashina Castle, the note is dropped by a Central Force Gunman near Anayama's shop.



## Overview[]

Contains a clue about the whereabouts of Flame Barrel, that unlocks the Flame Vent Prosthetic Tool when given to the Sculptor at the Dilapidated Temple. 

## Notes[]

  * Killing Anayama in the Hirata Estate, prior to its purchase, will make this item unobtainable for the rest of the playthrough.

**Senpou Monks** are a normal enemy in Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice. They are commonly found in Senpou Temple. 

## Melee Senpou Monk[]

## Melee Senpou Monk

Found patrolling and praying throughout Senpou Temple. 

### Behaviour and Tactics[]

  * **Senpou Style Martial Arts** : 
    * runs to the right and deliver a three hit combo.
    * a slow upward palm strike.
    * two spinning kicks.
    * runs forwards and does two spinning kicks, follows by an overhead kick.
    * Praying Strikes: an elbow strike, follows by a palm strike and a jumping kick.
  * **Throw Rock** : throws a rock at Wolf if he is too far away and out of reach.
  * **Perilous Grab** : readies in a stance while moving slowly towards Wolf. When near, dashes forward quickly elbow first and if connected, wrestles him onto the ground before stomping.



* * *

* * *

The monks in the courtyard are generally easier to defeat with stealth. However, their numbers can make confrontations difficult. Avoiding their grab is important, as it will deal severe damage if it lands.

## Adept Senpou Monk[]

## Adept Senpou Monk

Three found in the Temple Grounds at Senpou Temple. 

### Behaviour and Tactics[]

  * **Bomb Throw** : throws a small bomb adorned with grey feathers that slowly homes in on the Wolf, exploding after a short duration.
  * **Fist Strike** : strikes at Wolf with his fists.



* * *

At close range, they will defend themselves with their fists, blocking attacks and occasionally engaging in melee attacks. Relatively easy to defeat by simply repeatedly attacking.

## Dual Naginata Senpou Monk[]

## Dual Naginata Senpou Monk

Senpou Monk wearing a straw coat, large hat and wielding a double-blade Naginata. Three found in front of the Main Hall of the Senpou Temple. 

### Behaviour and Tactics[]

* **Somersault Shuriken Throw** : leaps backwards in a somersault, but also throwing two Shuriken in quick succession.
  * **Shuriken Throw** : chases after the target and throws two Shuriken.
  * **Blade Spin** : spins the blade from the right up to three times. May follow up with a Perilous Sting right after the second spin.
  * **Blade Spin Retreat** : spins the blade from the right twice and leaps backwards.
  * **Flying Pinwheel** : leaps high up then come spinning down at the target with incredible speed.
  * **Whirlwind Leap** : starts out in an arced run to the side, he leaps up and spins around in a whirlwind of attacks, and may followed up by another smaller whirlwind.
  * **Upperhead Cut** : using the Naginata as support, he pushes himself into the air then uses this momentum to strike with the blade. Sometimes followed up by a Shuriken Trow while mid-air.

* **Vault Over** : using the Naginata, he propels himself into the air, leaping behind his opponent. Often followed up by a Perilous Sting.
  * **Perilous Sting** : thrusts himself forward using the Naginata, travelling a great distance. Can be easily countered at the end of the attack.

* * *

Particularly vulnerable to being hit mid-air, either interrupting their attack, or allowing a Mid-air Deathblow.

## Khakkara Senpou Monk[]

## Khakkara Senpou Monk

A Senpou Monk wielding a ringed staff. Can be found in large numbers in the courtyard of Senpou Temple. 

### Behaviour and Tactics[]

  * **Swing** : crouches down to the left and swings once and may add another hit.
  * **Combo** : crouches down to the right and strikes with the hilt, follows by a roundhouse kick and another swing.
  * **Retreat** : strikes upward and leaping back a short distance.
  * **Leaping Smash** : plants the staff on the ground and uses it as a leaping point, he leaps up spinning and uses this momentum to smash down.
  * **Ungo's Sugar: **bites the candy and gains extra defense.
  * **Perilous Thrust** : quickly runs to the right and thrusts the staff forwards. He may turn around and thrusts once more.



* * *

* * *

When attacking them, they will always deflect the third attack and follow with a quick attack, and then with a Perilous Thrust.   


  * Melee & Adept

  * Naginata

  * Khakkara

## Trivia[]

  * The Khakkara is a Buddhist ringed staff used primarily in prayer or as a weapon. The jingling of the staff's rings was said to warn small sentient beings such as insects so they can avoid being accidentally trodden on, or to be used as a way to ask for help, if a monk was in need.
  * All the other monks can be _spirited away_ instantly using the Divine Abduction except for the Dual Naginata Senpou Monks.

  * Category:Prosthetic Combat Arts

A Shinobi Combat Art that allows one to perform a forward-dashing sword slice after using certain Prosthetic Tools, allowing one to close distance on enemies instantly. Applicable Prosthetic Tools: Loaded Shuriken, Shinobi Firecracker, Loaded Spear.   
---  
  
## Overview[]

The first Combat Art of the Prosthetic Arts tree, requires 11 Skill Points to unlock. The Prosthetic Arts tree requires Prosthetic Esoteric Text to unlock. 

## Ability[]

**(ATTACK after using Prosthetic Tools) Chasing Slice** : Take a leap forward and perform a wide slicing attack. 

Applicable Prosthetic Tools: 

  * Loaded Shuriken (after throwing)
  * Shinobi Firecrackers (after throwing)
  * Loaded Spear (after thrust/cleave)

After using certain Prosthetic Tools, this move allows one to attack with the Tool and sword simultaneously, or it provides a follow-up attack for the Tool. Applicable Prosthetic Tools: Loaded Axe, Loaded Spear, Mist Raven.   
---  
  
## Overview[]

A Combat Art of the Prosthetic Arts tree, requires 22 Skill Points to unlock. The Prosthetic Arts tree requires Prosthetic Esoteric Text to unlock. 

## Prerequisites[]

  * Chasing Slice



## Ability[]

**(ATTACK After using Prosthetic Tools) Fang and Blade** : Attack with the tool and sword simultaneously, or one after the other. 

Applicable Prosthetic Tools: 

  * Loaded Axe (after initial strike)
  * Loaded Spear (after dragging)
  * Mist Raven (after activating)

Uses the Grappling Hook to launch oneself at an enemy, and use that momentum to perform a rolling sword attack. The Shinobi Prosthetic is the perfect tool for combining movement and attack into one, ensuring no movement is wasted.   
---  
  
## Overview[]

The first Combat Art of the Prosthetic Arts tree, requires 11 Skill Points to unlock. The Prosthetic Arts tree requires Prosthetic Esoteric Text to unlock. 

## Ability[]

**(ATTACK during Grappling Hook movement) Grappling Hook Attack** : Use the forward momentum of your landing to perform a powerful sword attack.

A spinning leap attack that can quickly close or create distance from foes. A technique of the Nightjar Clan, the Shinobi who serve Ashina. The Nightjar use the weight of their massive shuriken to add force to the blow. The Shinobi Prosthetic is made of heavy steel and can be used in a similar capacity.   
---  
  
## Overview

A Combat Art of the Prosthetic Arts tree, requires 2 Skill Points to unlock. The Prosthetic Arts tree requires Prosthetic Esoteric Text to unlock. 

## Prerequisites[]

  * Grappling Hook Attack



## Ability[]

**(GUARD + ATTACK) Nightjar Slash** : Leap in with a spin and slash at the enemy.

Performs a spinning leap attack that can quickly close with or create distance from foes. This technique allows one to decide which direction to rotate in when performing Nightjar Slash. Making use of both directions makes this both an offensive and a defensive skill.   
---  
  
## Overview

A Combat Art of the Prosthetic Arts tree, requires 33 Skill Points to unlock. The Prosthetic Arts tree requires Prosthetic Esoteric Text to unlock. 

## Prerequisites[]

  * Grappling Hook Attack
  * Nightjar Slash



## Ability[]

**(GUARD + ATTACK) Nightjar Slash** : Leap in with a spin and slash away at the enemy. 

**(While locked on, hold movement against the direction of enemy, then GUARD + ATTACK) Reversal** : Slash at the target, then somersault away.

  * Snake Eyes Followers#Snake Eyes Cannoneer

The **Snake Eyes Followers** are a normal enemy in Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice. They are commonly found in Ashina Depths and Sunken Valley. 

## Snake Eyes Cannoneer[]

## Snake Eyes Cannoneer

Found in the poison pool of Ashina Depths, accompanying Snake Eyes Shirahagi. 

Also patrolling and guarding across Gun Fort. 

### Behaviour and Tactics[]

  * **Sommersault Cannon Shot** : swings the cannon, then rolls backwards or sideways, following up with a rapid shot.
  * **Cannon Swing** : swings the cannon in a wide angle.
  * **Side Roll Shot** : rolls to the side, following up with a cannon shot.
  * **Sprint Shot** : sprints to the side, abruptly stops and shoots once.
  * **Kick** : if attacked repeatedly, he kicks the attacker.



* * *

Watch out for his wide-spreading projectiles, and kicks when attacking. Try to stay behind him and try to keep him out of the poison pool if fighting the one right after the Ashina Depths Sculptor's Idol, and use the tent to block his projectiles.

### Loot[]

## Snake Eyes Spear-Bearer[]

## Snake Eyes Spear-Bearer

Found in the poison pool of Ashina Depths, accompanying Snake Eyes Shirahagi. 

### Behaviour and Tactics[]

  * **Kick** : kicks the attacker back, causing them to lose balance.
  * **Precise Shot** : stops to aim, then shoots a single, strong projectile from his spear-gun
  * **Fake Thrust Shot** : readies the spear as if to thrust, but shoots a projectile instead.
  * **Dodge** : dodges backwards, creating space between him and his attacker.
  * **Perilous Retaliation** : after blocking an attack, performs a fast, perilous thrusting attack with the spear.



* * *

Watch out for his Perilous Retaliation and Mikiri Counter it. Be careful as his kick has a rather wide area of effect. When he aims to shoot, if Wolf stands close enough to him, the projectile will not damage him.

### Burn[]  
  
---  
| Being hit by too many fire-based attacks will eventually apply the Burn status abnormality. Guarding fire attacks does not prevent the Burn gauge from rising. While burning, flames are visible on one's body, and will prevent the regeneration of Posture and will gradually damage Vitality for the duration.   
  
## Effect[]

Burn takes 1% Vitality per second for 10 seconds, for a total of 10% maximum Vitality. It also halts Posture recovery. 

## How to cure Burn[]

Burn takes 1% Vitality per second for 10 seconds, for a total of 10% maximum Vitality. It also halts Posture recovery. 

## How to cure Burn[]

  * Dousing Powder and Ministry Dousing Powder cure Burn and increase Burn resistance by 60%/80% for 30 seconds and reduce fire damage by 40/60%.
  * The Withered Red Gourd, while it doesn't heal active Burn status abnormality, increases Burn resistance by 70% for 30 seconds and reduces fire damage by 50%.
  * Divine Grass cures Burn and fully restores Vitality.

### Poison[]  
  
---  
| Repeatedly getting hit by poison-based attacks will apply the "Poison" status abnormality. Guarding such attacks does not prevent Poison from accumulating. Poison affects the body and mind when it enters the body, gradually reducing Vitality over time.   
  
## Effect[]

Poison is a status effect that lasts for 40 seconds. Depending on the amount of maximum vitality, it can deplete from a third to almost the entire vitality. 

## How to cure Poison[]

  * Antidote Powder cures Poison and increases Poison resistance by 70% for 30 seconds.
  * The Green Mossy Gourd, while it doesn't heal active Poison status abnormality, increases Poison resistance by 70% for 30 seconds.
  * Divine Grass cures Poison and fully restores Vitality.
  * Contact Medicine inflicts a weak form of Poison, making others ineffective.

  * Lizard

## How to cure Terror[]

Terror is a lethal status effect that will kill Sekiro once the status gauge is full.

### Shock[]  
  
---  
| If standing on the ground while struck by a lightning attack, the status abnormality "Shock" is inflicted. This occurs regardless of whether the attack was guarded or not. Shock causes electricity to run through one's body, dealing huge damage to Vitality and also stunning them briefly.   
  
## Effect[]

If Sekiro's feet are on the ground and he takes a lightning attack, he will take a massive Vitality and Posture damage, the amount of which varies depending on his vitality. 

## How to cure Shock[]

  * Eel Liver cures Shock and increases Shock resistance by 50% for 30 seconds.
  * Divine Grass cures Shock and fully restores Vitality.

## How to inflict Shock[]

#### Lightning Reversal:[]

### Enfeeblement[]  
  
---  
| Syphons youth out of the target, restricting his agile movements to only a slow limping, weak attack and the inability to use any items or prosthetic tools. It also greatly reduces his health and disables resurrection.   
  
## Effect[]

Enfeeblement is an unique statues effect inflicted by only one enemy. When the status gauge is full from playing the flute, Sekiro becomes old and infirm, unable to use prosthetics or items, with low health and weak attack. If killed, Sekiro can't resurrect. Once cured, the full health gauge is restored but low health remains. 

## How to cure Enfeeblement[]

## How to cure Enfeeblement[]

  * Kill the Palace Noble that inflicted it and perform a Deathblow on him.
  * Wait for its effect to run out (30 seconds).
  * Reaching a Sculptor's Idol and resting.



## Enemies that inflict Enfeeblement[]

  * Palace Noble

## Yari Monk

**Shinobi Hunters** are a normal enemy in Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice. They are yari-wielding monks. 

## Location[]

  * Old Grave: One is found near the Sculptor's Idol with an Ashina swordsman near him. Can be eavesdropped after the **Central Forces** invasion.
  * Hirata Estate: Two are found at the end of a side path, which begins near the bottom of the vertical shaft before the Hirata Estate - Main Hall idol. Rewards a Bulging Coin Purse when both are defeated.

### Burn[]  
  
---  
| Being hit by too many fire-based attacks will eventually apply the Burn status abnormality. Guarding fire attacks does not prevent the Burn gauge from rising. While burning, flames are visible on one's body, and will prevent the regeneration of Posture and will gradually damage Vitality for the duration.   
  
## Effect[]

Burn takes 1% Vitality per second for 10 seconds, for a total of 10% maximum Vitality. It also halts Posture recovery. 

## How to cure Burn[]

Burn takes 1% Vitality per second for 10 seconds, for a total of 10% maximum Vitality. It also halts Posture recovery. 

## How to cure Burn[]

  * Dousing Powder and Ministry Dousing Powder cure Burn and increase Burn resistance by 60%/80% for 30 seconds and reduce fire damage by 40/60%.
  * The Withered Red Gourd, while it doesn't heal active Burn status abnormality, increases Burn resistance by 70% for 30 seconds and reduces fire damage by 50%.
  * Divine Grass cures Burn and fully restores Vitality.



## Enemies that inflict Burn[]

  * Torch-Wielding Bandit
  * Archer Bandit
  * Black Nightjar
  * Lesser Centipede
  * Central Force Flametrooper

### Poison[]  
  
---  
| Repeatedly getting hit by poison-based attacks will apply the "Poison" status abnormality. Guarding such attacks does not prevent Poison from accumulating. Poison affects the body and mind when it enters the body, gradually reducing Vitality over time.   
  
## Effect[]

Poison is a status effect that lasts for 40 seconds. Depending on the amount of maximum vitality, it can deplete from a third to almost the entire vitality. 

## How to cure Poison[]

  * Antidote Powder cures Poison and increases Poison resistance by 70% for 30 seconds.
  * The Green Mossy Gourd, while it doesn't heal active Poison status abnormality, increases Poison resistance by 70% for 30 seconds.
  * Divine Grass cures Poison and fully restores Vitality.
  * Contact Medicine inflicts a weak form of Poison, making others ineffective.



## Enemies that inflict Poison[]

  * Lizard
  * Rat
  * Archer Bandit (Altered Hirata Estate memory only)
  * Interior Ministry Agent

### Terror[]  
  
---  
| Taking damage from apparition-type enemies will fill the mind and body with Terror. Guarding such attacks does not prevent Terror from accumulating. Those overcome with Terror are known to die.   
  
## Effect[]

Terror is a lethal status effect that will kill Sekiro once the status gauge is full. 

## How to cure Terror[]

Terror is a lethal status effect that will kill Sekiro once the status gauge is full. 

## How to cure Terror[]

  * The Mottled Purple Gourd cures Terror build-up and increases Terror resistance by 50% for 30 seconds.

### Shock[]  
  
---  
| If standing on the ground while struck by a lightning attack, the status abnormality "Shock" is inflicted. This occurs regardless of whether the attack was guarded or not. Shock causes electricity to run through one's body, dealing huge damage to Vitality and also stunning them briefly.   
  
## Effect[]

If Sekiro's feet are on the ground and he takes a lightning attack, he will take a massive Vitality and Posture damage, the amount of which varies depending on his vitality. 

## How to cure Shock[]

  * Eel Liver cures Shock and increases Shock resistance by 50% for 30 seconds.
  * Divine Grass cures Shock and fully restores Vitality.



## Enemies that inflict Shock[]

#### Lightning Reversal:[]

## How to inflict Shock[]

#### Lightning Reversal:[]

Lightning surges through the bodies of those with their feet on the ground, instantly paralyzing them. A secret technique exists to catch lightning in one's blade while in mid-air, and send it back.

### Enfeeblement[]  
  
---  
| Syphons youth out of the target, restricting his agile movements to only a slow limping, weak attack and the inability to use any items or prosthetic tools. It also greatly reduces his health and disables resurrection.   
  
## Effect[]

Enfeeblement is an unique statues effect inflicted by only one enemy. When the status gauge is full from playing the flute, Sekiro becomes old and infirm, unable to use prosthetics or items, with low health and weak attack. If killed, Sekiro can't resurrect. Once cured, the full health gauge is restored but low health remains. 

## How to cure Enfeeblement[]

## How to cure Enfeeblement[]

  * Kill the Palace Noble that inflicted it and perform a Deathblow on him.
  * Wait for its effect to run out (30 seconds).
  * Reaching a Sculptor's Idol and resting.



## Enemies that inflict Enfeeblement[]

  * Palace Noble

## Description[]

**Monkeys** are a normal enemy in Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice. They are commonly found in Ashina Castle, Ashina Depths and Sunken Valley. 

## Monkey[]

## Monkey

Three found on the grassy road towards the Great Serpent Shrine; two in the tall grass and one sitting atop a torii. 

Several found on the right path leading down from Temple Grounds in Senpou Temple, accompanied by a Mallet-Wielding Taro Soldier Soldier. 

Several of them, some wielding a rifle or a sword are sitting on a small island in the poison pools of Riven Cave along with a Monkey Warrior. 

### Behaviour and Tactics[]

### Unarmed Monkey[]

While they are not much of a threat to Wolf by themselves, they usually always attack in groups. They can also throw dirt/rocks at Wolf and if he gets hit, he will be stunned. All monkeys are easily dealt with Spinning Shuriken or Flame Vent. The are also easily intimidated by Shinobi Firecracker. The Finger Whistle can also turn them against each other.

### Sword-Wielding Monkey[]

The Sword-Wielding Monkeys are the most dangerous and quickly can shorten the distance between them and Wolf with a few agile jumps. They have a five-hit combo that if it lands can deal a significant damage. They are also able to defend against Wolf's katana, however since they have low Vitality and Posture, they can be overwhelmed easily. If Wolf evades them for a while and keeps its distance, the monkeys get frustrated and will throw their katana at him, making them unarmed. 

### Rifle-Wielding Monkey[]

The Rifle-Wielding Monkeys will always try to keep their distance from Wolf. After each three shots, they take some time to reload. If they can't escape Wolf, they will try to chase him away with few swipes or with an overhead slam from their rifle. The slam will cause the rifle to explode dealing damage to anything nearby, but making the monkeys become unarmed. 

  


  * Sunken Valley, Senpou Temple

  * Ashina Castle (Second Invasion)

## Monkey Warrior[]

## Monkey Warrior

A white Monkey wielding double katana. 

Two of them found in Riven Cave, one standing by itself before the Toxic Memorial Mob, and another sitting on a small island in the poison pool, along with Monkeys wielding a rifle or a sword. Another two can be found near the Great Serpent Shrine Idol after the Interior Ministry's final invasion. 

### Behaviour and Tactics[]

  * **Perilous Sweep** : sweeps the ground with both katanas.
  * **Swipes** : two horizontal slashes.
  * **Retreat** : jumps back, slashing at the same time.
  * **Jumping Smash** : jumps up then comes smashing down.
  * **Flurry** : jumps back and initiates a rapid combo of 5 slashes, may ends with a last jumping smash.

## Upper Tower[]

A series of rooms in the central tower, not limited to the Dojo where Isshin's pupils train, the living quarters of the Divine Heir, Kuro and the sick room of Isshin Ashina himself. 

A hanging scroll in the Dojo tells of an old battle with ghosts that lurked the lands of Ashina and employed the lightning of the Fountainhead gods, hinting at later events.

After the first invasion, an ogre has been brought into the main hall, but is just one of many formidable foes Sekiro must face as he approaches the upper reaches of the castle. 

During the final invasion, the young lord, Kuro has fled the castle, and Emma remains in his room with the recently deceased Isshin Ashina. She gives the Wolf a key to the secret passage in the Reservoir and tells him to meet Kuro there.

## Ashina Reservoir and Secret Passage[]

The reservoir is the main water supply for the castle. Beneath the bridge, there is a secret passage leading outside the walls of Ashina Castle. 

The reservoir appears to be the invaders' entry point; many wooden ladders were placed to allow entrance to the castle. 

During the final invasion, Kuro once again awaits Wolf in the silvergrass field past the secret passage at the bottom of the Reservoir. This is also the site of the final confrontation with Genichiro Ashina.

## Description[]

## In-Game Description[]

Unleashes repeated attacks, overwhelming enemies with flowing, dance-like movements.   
While an Ashina Combat Art, it was taught by an outsider, and as such is considered heretical.   
The master of this technique crossed the Floating Passage and descended to Ashina.   
Her name was Tomoe.   
---  
  
## Availability[]

  * Unlocked by acquiring the Floating Passage Text from Pot Noble Harunaga in Hirata Estate for 5 5\. 
    * If Koremori's Truly Precious Bait has been fed to the Great Coloured Carp, he'll now sell the Floating Passage Text in the Fountainhead Palace.



## Overview[]

Deals a quick string of hits that partially go through an enemy's defense, making it ideal against regular humanoid foes, but can be interrupted if one bruteforces through it with an heavy blow. 

## Ability[]

**(GUARD + ATTACK then ATTACK then ATTACK) Floating Passage** : Deliver five dancing, consecutive attacks. 

## Notes[]

## Ability[]

**(GUARD + ATTACK then ATTACK then ATTACK) Floating Passage** : Deliver five dancing, consecutive attacks. 

## Notes[]

  * Purchasing the Floating Passage Text will also make the Spiral Cloud Passage Combat Art available for acquisition among the Mushin Esoteric Text Skill Tree.



## Trivia[]

  * The only Combat Art that doesn't belong in any Skill Tree.
  * Since Genichiro uses this same move, it has probably been passed down to him by his mentor Tomoe.

Game Mechanics • Combat Mechanics • **Status Effects** • New Game Plus • Attack Power • Skill Experience  
---  
Bosses | Enemies | Prosthetic Tools | Combat Arts  
  
### Burn[]  
  
---  
| Being hit by too many fire-based attacks will eventually apply the Burn status abnormality. Guarding fire attacks does not prevent the Burn gauge from rising. While burning, flames are visible on one's body, and will prevent the regeneration of Posture and will gradually damage Vitality for the duration.   
  
## Effect[]

Burn takes 1% Vitality per second for 10 seconds, for a total of 10% maximum Vitality. It also halts Posture recovery. 

## How to cure Burn[]

Burn takes 1% Vitality per second for 10 seconds, for a total of 10% maximum Vitality. It also halts Posture recovery. 

## How to cure Burn[]

  * Dousing Powder and Ministry Dousing Powder cure Burn and increase Burn resistance by 60%/80% for 30 seconds and reduce fire damage by 40/60%.
  * The Withered Red Gourd, while it doesn't heal active Burn status abnormality, increases Burn resistance by 70% for 30 seconds and reduces fire damage by 50%.
  * Divine Grass cures Burn and fully restores Vitality.



## Enemies that inflict Burn[]

  * Torch-Wielding Bandit
  * Archer Bandit
  * Black Nightjar
  * Lesser Centipede
  * Central Force Flametrooper

## Enemies that are weak to Burn[]

### Bosses[]

  * Demon of Hatred

## How to inflict Burn[]

  * Flame Vent: 
    * An enemy covered in Oil is more susceptible to Burn.
    * The Fire effect of the Flame Vent can be applied to the Kusabimaru by unlocking the Living Force Combat Art.

### Poison[]  
  
---  
| Repeatedly getting hit by poison-based attacks will apply the "Poison" status abnormality. Guarding such attacks does not prevent Poison from accumulating. Poison affects the body and mind when it enters the body, gradually reducing Vitality over time.   
  
## Effect[]

Poison is a status effect that lasts for 40 seconds. Depending on the amount of maximum vitality, it can deplete from a third to almost the entire vitality. 

## How to cure Poison[]

  * Antidote Powder cures Poison and increases Poison resistance by 70% for 30 seconds.
  * The Green Mossy Gourd, while it doesn't heal active Poison status abnormality, increases Poison resistance by 70% for 30 seconds.
  * Divine Grass cures Poison and fully restores Vitality.
  * Contact Medicine inflicts a weak form of Poison, making others ineffective.



## Enemies that inflict Poison[]

  * Lizard
  * Rat
  * Archer Bandit (Altered Hirata Estate memory only)
  * Interior Ministry Agent

## Effect[]

Terror is a lethal status effect that will kill Sekiro once the status gauge is full. 

## How to cure Terror[]

Terror is a lethal status effect that will kill Sekiro once the status gauge is full.

### Shock[]  
  
---  
| If standing on the ground while struck by a lightning attack, the status abnormality "Shock" is inflicted. This occurs regardless of whether the attack was guarded or not. Shock causes electricity to run through one's body, dealing huge damage to Vitality and also stunning them briefly.   
  
## Effect[]

If Sekiro's feet are on the ground and he takes a lightning attack, he will take a massive Vitality and Posture damage, the amount of which varies depending on his vitality. 

## How to cure Shock[]

  * Eel Liver cures Shock and increases Shock resistance by 50% for 30 seconds.
  * Divine Grass cures Shock and fully restores Vitality.



## Enemies that inflict Shock[]

  * Okami Swordsman
  * Okami Juggler
  * Palace Dog



### Mini-Bosses[]

  * Okami Leader Shizu



### Bosses[]

  * Genichiro Ashina (Phase 3 only)
  * Genichiro, the Way of Tomoe
  * Isshin, the Sword Saint (Phase 3 only)



## How to inflict Shock[]

#### Lightning Reversal:[]

## How to inflict Shock[]

#### Lightning Reversal:[]

Lightning surges through the bodies of those with their feet on the ground, instantly paralyzing them. A secret technique exists to catch lightning in one's blade while in mid-air, and send it back.   
---  
  
### Enfeeblement[]  
  
---  
| Syphons youth out of the target, restricting his agile movements to only a slow limping, weak attack and the inability to use any items or prosthetic tools. It also greatly reduces his health and disables resurrection.   
  
## Effect[]

Enfeeblement is an unique statues effect inflicted by only one enemy. When the status gauge is full from playing the flute, Sekiro becomes old and infirm, unable to use prosthetics or items, with low health and weak attack. If killed, Sekiro can't resurrect. Once cured, the full health gauge is restored but low health remains. 

## How to cure Enfeeblement[]

## How to cure Enfeeblement[]

  * Kill the Palace Noble that inflicted it and perform a Deathblow on him.
  * Wait for its effect to run out (30 seconds).
  * Reaching a Sculptor's Idol and resting.



## Enemies that inflict Enfeeblement[]

  * Palace Noble



### Red-Eyes[]  
  
---  
| Those with Red Eyes are dangerous and filled with rage, and attempting to defeat them in hand-to-hand combat seems unwise. Fire, however, is very effective against them. They are said to fear fire above all else.   
  
## Enemies with Red-Eyes[]

  * Grey Nightjar
  * Red-Eyed Carp
  * Jinzaemon Kumano (if sent to Doujun)
  * Kotaro (if sent to Doujun)
  * Doujun (at the end of his questline)



### Mini-bosses[]

  * Chained Ogre
  * Ashina Elite - Ujinari Mizuo



## How to gain Red-Eyes[]

  * Consume a Red Lump.

### Burn[]  
  
---  
| Being hit by too many fire-based attacks will eventually apply the Burn status abnormality. Guarding fire attacks does not prevent the Burn gauge from rising. While burning, flames are visible on one's body, and will prevent the regeneration of Posture and will gradually damage Vitality for the duration.   
  
## Effect[]

Burn takes 1% Vitality per second for 10 seconds, for a total of 10% maximum Vitality. It also halts Posture recovery. 

## How to cure Burn[]

Burn takes 1% Vitality per second for 10 seconds, for a total of 10% maximum Vitality. It also halts Posture recovery. 

## How to cure Burn[]

  * Dousing Powder and Ministry Dousing Powder cure Burn and increase Burn resistance by 60%/80% for 30 seconds and reduce fire damage by 40/60%.
  * The Withered Red Gourd, while it doesn't heal active Burn status abnormality, increases Burn resistance by 70% for 30 seconds and reduces fire damage by 50%.
  * Divine Grass cures Burn and fully restores Vitality.



## Enemies that inflict Burn[]

  * Torch-Wielding Bandit
  * Archer Bandit

  * Lesser Centipede
  * Central Force Flametrooper

Enfeeblement

Enfeeblement

An ancient kodachi short sword, its blade mottled with bluish rust. Can be fitted to the Shinobi Prosthetic to create a Prothetic Tool.  
Forged by the Ashina clan to resist the inhuman evil that had invaded Ashina in times long forgotten. It was the poisonous gift of the blue rust that finally drove the spirits out.  |   
---|---  
  
Found in a chest in the lower part of the Upper Tower - Antechamber of the Ashina Castle. A clue about its whereabouts is sold by Fujioka the Info Broker for 500 500\. 

Unlocks the Sabimaru Prosthetic Tool when given to the Sculptor at the Dilapidated Temple.
